title: Function Declarations and Definitions
learningObjectives: Identify the function's role, inputs and control flow.
Trace calls, local state and returned results.
Recognize common design or safety mistakes.
Write and test a reusable function for a practical task.

understand.concept: A function declaration introduces a function name, return type and parameter list. A definition provides its body. A declaration must be visible before a call is compiled; a definition must be available to the linker.
understand.whyItMatters: Functions break a large program into named, reusable units. Separating declaration from definition lets callers use a function without seeing its implementation.
understand.explain: Read a function signature from left to right: return type, name, parameters. Compare the prototype and definition carefully; they must match. A function definition may appear before main or after main when a declaration is provided first.

examples.title: Prototype before main
examples.code: int square(int value);\nint main(){return square(4)==16?0:1;}\nint square(int value){return value*value;}
examples.explanation: The declaration makes square known at the call; the later definition supplies its body.

examples.title: Simple reusable helper
examples.code: int clampLow(int n){return n<0?0:n;}\n// clampLow(-3) -> 0; clampLow(8) -> 8
examples.explanation: The helper expresses one operation and can be called repeatedly.

examples.title: Two functions compose
examples.code: int twice(int n){return n*2;}\nint addOne(int n){return n+1;}\n// addOne(twice(3)) -> 7
examples.explanation: The returned value of one function can be passed to another.

examples.title: Function call chain
examples.code: int square(int x){return x*x;}\nint sumSquares(int a,int b){return square(a)+square(b);}
examples.explanation: sumSquares uses a helper instead of repeating multiplication logic.

examples.title: Matching prototype and definition
examples.code: bool isEven(int n);\nbool isEven(int n){return n%2==0;}
examples.explanation: Declaration and definition share the same return type and parameters.

practise.guidedTask: Walk through all five Function Declarations and Definitions examples. Annotate the signature, call arguments, local state, control flow, return behavior and side effects.
practise.independentTask: Create a small utilities file with at least three prototypes and matching definitions. Call the helpers from main and confirm each signature matches.
hints: Start with the function signature and intended contract.
Trace each call with a small input.
Separate calculation from output when appropriate.
Test normal, boundary and invalid cases.
Check lifetimes, side effects and termination.

questions.explanation: A function declaration introduces its signature.

questions.prompt: When can a call use a function defined later?
questions.explanation: A prior declaration makes the signature visible.

questions.prompt: Prototype and definition must match in?
questions.explanation: The function signature must be consistent.
Helpers separate responsibilities and can be tested independently.
The body is the code executed by the function.
